title: Ad Click Event Aggregation
oneLine: Keep an immutable raw click log, aggregate by event time with watermarks and dedupe, publish queryable windows, and reconcile stream results against a batch source of truth.
opening: Because clicks drive billing, I would preserve every accepted raw event in an immutable partitioned log and treat aggregates as derived views. Edge collectors validate schema, attach event/ingest timestamps and a click ID, then publish by ad or campaign key. A stream processor deduplicates, applies fraud signals, and aggregates tumbling or sliding windows using event time. Watermarks decide when a window is complete while allowing bounded late events; later corrections update a versioned aggregate. Results go to an OLAP/query store, while raw events remain in object storage for replay and audit. A periodic batch reconciliation recomputes authoritative totals and emits adjustments rather than silently rewriting billed history. Hot campaigns are salted or two-stage aggregated.
ask: Is this for dashboards, billing, fraud, attribution, or all?
How late can events arrive and how exact must counts be?
What is the duplicate/fraud model and retention requirement?
scale: 1B clicks/day is roughly 11.6K/s average; campaign peaks and bot attacks can be orders of magnitude higher.
Dimension combinations define aggregate cardinality; precompute only common cubes and use OLAP for flexible drill-down.
Raw log retention enables replay after code/fraud-rule changes and is mandatory when money depends on the result.

decisions.default: Event time with watermarks and an explicit allowed-lateness policy.
decisions.why: Processing-time windows misattribute delayed mobile/offline events.
decisions.switch: Processing time is adequate for purely operational live dashboards where exact attribution is irrelevant.

decisions.default: Streaming for freshness plus immutable raw replay and periodic reconciliation.
decisions.why: This combines low latency with an auditable correction path.
decisions.switch: Kappa-style replay from one log can simplify code if one stream engine handles historical backfill safely.

decisions.default: Stable click/event ID with state TTL and idempotent aggregate updates.
decisions.why: Network/client retries are normal and billing cannot double count them.
decisions.switch: Approximate structures may be acceptable for non-billing analytics at massive scale.

decisions.default: Two-stage aggregation with deterministic salt for hot campaigns, then merge.
decisions.why: One popular ad should not serialize the whole stream on one partition.
decisions.switch: Preserve strict per-key order only where the computation genuinely requires it.

deepDives.title: Watermarks and late data
points: Watermark estimates that events before time T are mostly complete.
Keep window state for allowed lateness and emit updates/retractions with version.
Very late events flow into reconciliation/adjustment rather than unbounded online state.

deepDives.title: Exactly-once accounting
points: Checkpoint source offsets and operator state atomically in the stream engine.
Write aggregates idempotently with window/key/version or transactional sink.
Billing still uses finalized/reconciled ledger entries, not a vague ‘exactly once’ claim.

deepDives.title: Fraud and audit
points: Keep raw event, validation decision, rule/model version, and provenance.
Separate observed clicks from billable clicks.
Corrections are append-only adjustments with a reason and lineage.

failures.response: Restore checkpoint, replay log from offsets, and use idempotent/versioned sink.

failures.risk: Late events change a billed period
failures.response: Finalize after policy cutoff; post an adjustment event and preserve both original and corrected totals.
Salt/two-stage aggregate, pre-aggregate at edge, and rebalance based on measured key skew.
Immutable raw archive, versioned jobs, shadow recomputation, and controlled replay/backfill.

questions.a: Event time answers when the click occurred and needs watermarks for out-of-order arrivals. Processing time answers when the system saw it and is simpler but can put delayed events in the wrong business window.
A progress estimate used to close event-time windows. It is not a guarantee that no earlier event will arrive; allowed lateness and correction policy handle exceptions.

questions.q: How do you get exactly one billed click?
questions.a: Stable event ID, dedupe, checkpointed processing, idempotent/versioned aggregate writes, and final append-only billing ledger/reconciliation. Define the boundary instead of relying on broker marketing terminology.

questions.q: Why keep raw data if aggregates exist?
questions.a: For audit, fraud reclassification, bug recovery, new dimensions, and deterministic replay. Aggregates are a replaceable view; raw accepted facts are the evidence.

mistakes: Using processing time for financial attribution without discussion
Ignoring late corrections and billing finalization
Partitioning solely by campaign when a campaign can be extremely hot
seniorSignal: Connect streaming semantics to financial correctness. Explain event time, finalization, append-only adjustments, replay lineage, and the exact boundary of dedupe/transactions.
implementation: Kafka with schema registry and immutable object-store archive
Flink/Kafka Streams event-time windows, checkpoints, and keyed state
Batch reconciliation job and append-only billing adjustment ledger
